newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey accepts 30-year lease bids for seven ports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey accepts 30-year lease bids for seven ports.

text.p: Turkey has accepted leases for the operation of seven Turkish ports over a 30-year period for a total $252.3 million, the Privatisation Administration (OIB) has announced.
The final decision on the leasing of the seven ports, currently run by Turkey's shipping authority, will be presented to the High Privatisation Board for approval.
The OIB accepted bids for the ports of Antalya, Giresun, Hopa, Ordu, Rize, Tekirdag and Sinop. It did not accept bids which were also made for Trabzon port.

A bid by Trakya Port Operations of $134.6 million was accepted for Tekirdag port, while Link Import-Export's bid of $102.5 million was accepted for Antalya port. The cheapest accepted bid, of just under $801,000, was accepted for Sinop.
About 300 workers in total are employed at the seven leased ports.
Privatisation officials say that if the leasing of these small and medium-sized ports is successful then a similar arrangement for larger ports will be put on the agenda.
